content.thinking: I'm fixing the root cause by describing each usage per row rather than naming the revision. The reconcile step compares against the sum of purchases, which is the check that actually caught this. I'm also checking whether step 4 of the chain has the same problem and will adjust it to be accurate per row.

action_items.item: After the rollback, rewrite the stored month total of every account written since the deploy so it matches its current-month purchases. Take the export in the same month as the repair.
Run the spend-integrity reconciliation automatically after every deploy of io-shop, not only on its weekly schedule.
Add a check on the purchase write path that flags an account whose stored month total disagrees with its current-month purchases right after it is written.
Require any change that stops writing a stored field to list the code that uses that field, and to show each use moved off it, before it is merged.
Make a passing run of the io-shop test suite a required gate before any revision is deployed from the deploy/ directory.
Route SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile to the io-shop on-call rotation so that it pages a person.

causal_chain.step: The saved month totals of the shoppers checked no longer matched the purchases recorded against them. The spend-integrity check found this, not any shopper report.

Purchases recorded at the running revision were added to the account and to its lifetime total, but the stored month total was left unchanged. Both write paths in the file behave this way: record_purchase and record_purchase_deriving_the_month.

ruled_out.what: The earlier deploy of 4c810f22894e612ced87f5ee3f3062dfeb785050: the alert dates the oldest affected purchase at {A4}, after the later deploy of 26f1d7e at {P2.1}.
A flag change: the flag provider showed no flag changes by anyone but Argus in the hour before the onset.

causal_chain.step: Revision 26f1d7e2c82ce2abff8f9b6424dc226f4f37fed2, deployed to io-shop at {P2.1}, removed the conditional total_this_month_cents update from record_purchase. All {T10.2} replicas were running it as of {T10.1}.

The change stopped keeping the stored month total up to date, but other code still uses that stored field. The monthly statement reads it as the month total, the spend summaries divide it by the number of purchases, and the reconciliation compares it with the sum of the month's purchases.

input.cause_in_plain_words: A code change stopped the shop updating each shopper's saved total for this month's spending when they bought something, but the parts of the shop that show and check that total still read the saved figure.

contributing_factors.factor: The only check seen that compares stored month totals with purchases is the spend-integrity check, which runs every {A5} days. The write path itself does not notice the two drifting apart.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A check that ran soon after each deploy, or after each write, would have caught the first short total soon after the deploy instead of {alerted_after_the_onset} later, which would have shortened how long bad totals kept being written.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: Before the deploy, no check was seen that the code still using total_this_month_cents had been moved off it. The change says the month adds up from the purchase history, but the statement and spend-summary code still use the stored field.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A review that listed the users of the dropped field would have shown them still reading it, and the change would have been held back or that code changed first.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: No test run blocking the deploy was seen. Code-Fix reports that the test file at the running revision holds a test that the month is added to the total record_purchase receives, which the deployed record_purchase no longer does.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A required test run before deploying would have stopped the revision from going out.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: The SpendTotalsDoNotReconcile alert paged nobody: no on-call incident was linked to it.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A paged person could have done the recommended rollback once the alert fired, which would have stopped more bad totals being written sooner.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent read what the deployment of 26f1d7e changed, which pointed straight at the removed month-total update.
Argus did not act on C1 when nothing could tell whether the action had worked, and recommended the rollback to a person instead.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #429.

input.root_cause: The change removed the total_this_month_cents update from record_purchase, and the other write path, record_purchase_deriving_the_month, does not move it either, so every purchase was added to the account while the stored month total stayed where it was. Code that uses the stored field still reads it as kept up to date: render_monthly_statement reads it as the month total, and average_spend_per_item_this_month and the_mean_purchase_this_month divide it by the number of purchases this month. The total therefore no longer matches the current-month purchases that reconcile_monthly_totals compares it against.
input.still_at_risk: Until a person rolls io-shop back, every new purchase can leave another shopper's saved month total short of what they bought, and the totals already written wrong stay wrong on statements and spend summaries until someone rewrites them.
input.symptom: Shoppers' saved spend-this-month totals fell short of their actual purchases
